name: Macintosh IIci ROM 368CADFE - PiStorm/Emu68 patches
notes: the four dbf loops at 0x40800880/88E/8A4/8BC count down d0.w from 0xFFFF until VIA1
timer 2 interrupts (vector $64 -> 0x40800866 -> jmp (a2)) or d0.w wraps to -1 after
65536 iterations (dbf falls through -> jmp (a2)).  The shared continuation at
0x4080084E does not.w d0, which turns the fall-through value 0xFFFF into 0, i.e. a
very fast CPU stores TimeDBRA = 0 and every derived delay collapses.  Fix: a2 points
to a 10-byte stub in the 14 bytes of zero padding after the last loop (0x408008D2,
nothing references it; the next routine 0x408008E0 is reached by braw from 0x408000B4)
that performs not.w d0 and turns a zero result into 0xFFFF (saturate), then branches
to 0x40800850 (the store).  Normal (slow-CPU) results are unchanged.

Second stub (16 Nov, later): the Pi supplies the calibration results. At JIT speed the CPU loop (TimeDBRA) overflows and the bus loops (TimeSCSIDB/TimeVIADB/TimeSCCDB) measure the bridge latency, which can leave absurd timeout counts (a saturated TimeSCSIDB made a SCSI wait last 48 minutes). The stub looks the loop's low-memory address up in a table at the slot-9 window + 0x80 (psmb.h PSMB_OFF_CALIB: 4 x {address.w, value.w}) that the kernel fills from its own measurements, and falls back to saturation when the window is absent or the entry is 0.

Boot time (19 Nov 2026, docs/08 item 50): the cold-start RAM test and the startup chime are cut short. The RAM test (moving inversions over every memory chunk, $408446BC, called from StartTest at $408436BE) tests the Pi's own RAM, which cannot fail as SIMMs do, and took most of the ROM's own start; sizing is a separate routine ($408431C0, d7 = 17) and runs as before, the warm-start path (Restart) never ran the test at all, and no later test reads what it leaves in memory. The chime's length is the outer count of its wavetable loop (30000 steps of 14 VIA reads each); nothing plays the ASC on an SE or a bare Pi, so it was half a second to a second of silence. The SCSI Manager's selection timeout ($62 of its globals, 250 ms, set at $40809554) is 10 ms: every empty SCSI ID cost the full timeout at each scan, twice per boot, about three seconds with one disk; a target must answer its selection within 200 microseconds (the SCSI standard's selection abort time), so 10 ms is fifty times that.

Memory Manager, a freed or bad pointer in 32-bit mode (21 Nov 2026, docs/08 item 78): the dispatchers for the calls that take a pointer ($4080DC2E, through $1EE4: DisposPtr and three others) or a handle ($4080DC6E, through $1EEC) check the block in the current layout ($1EFC bit 0: 32-bit) and, if that check fails, check it again in the other layout, with the address masked to 24 bits. With more than 16 MB that masked address is another block of RAM, and a uniform fill there ($55 on the user's SE) passes the 24-bit check by coincidence: the dispatcher then jumps through the fill to $FFFFFFFF (Speedometer 3.23 disposing a pointer twice). In 32-bit mode (MMU32Bit $CB2 set) a pointer or handle whose high byte is not zero cannot belong to a 24-bit zone, so its 24-bit retry is skipped and the 32-bit check's error (-111, -113) is returned, as a Mac with 16 MB or less always does. 24-bit mode and pointers below 16 MB retry exactly as before.

The 400K drive's speed (25 Nov 2026, docs/08 item 146): the IIci ROM's Sony driver has dropped the 400K drive's speed control (FigTrkSpd $4086D7F0 and SetSpeed $4086CB60 are stubs), and on the 128K and 512K that drive takes its speed from the low bytes of the sound buffer, which nothing writes. Every seek of the driver goes through a 10-byte wrapper at $4086D4B0 (bclr #11,d6; move.l JSeek,-(sp); rts: the SE ROM's $4350DE with its call of SetSpeed taken out; called from $4086CC98, $4086CCA8, $4086D144 and $4086EA68), so the wrapper jumps to a stub in the zero padding at 0x62AC0 that does what it did and, when the Pi's window says the kernel wants it (psmb.h struct psmb_floppy, 'SP' at window+$90), puts the track there, counts the seek, and for a seek into another zone (16 tracks) sets the driver's own speed-change wait (SonyVars+20, which Seek still waits out for a 400K drive at $4086D512) to the kernel's wait per zone times the zones moved, at most the driver's longest (SonyVars+56, 400 ms). The kernel writes the drive's pulse widths into the low bytes (psmac_board_se.c). Without the window, or with 'SP' absent (every board but the 128K and 512K unless mac.floppyspeed=on), the stub only does the wrapper's two instructions.

patches.name: calib: point a2 (loop continuation) at the stub in the padding gap
calib: the 14-byte gap only holds a long branch to the real stub
asm: bra.l   calib_stub2     | 68020 long branch: the stub is 400 KB away

patches.name: calib: stub in the zero padding at 0x629E0: take the value from the Pi's table, else saturate
asm: not.w   %d0             | d0.w = iterations completed (0 if dbf fell through)
cmp.l   #0x50534D42,(%a1) | 'PSMB': is the Pi's window there?
cmpa.w  (%a4),%a0       | (a4) = this loop's low-memory address (TimeDBRA, TimeSCCDB, TimeSCSIDB, TimeVIADB)
3:      jmp calib_store:l     | -> 0x40800850: move.w d0 to the low-memory global

patches.name: boot: skip the cold-start RAM test (StartTest's call of $408446BC: bra.s to its return point)
boot: the startup chime's wavetable loop runs 2 steps instead of 30000 (its table at $40807158, the outer count)
boot: SCSI selection timeout 10 ms instead of 250 ms (the SCSI Manager's default, $62 of its globals)
mm: the pointer dispatcher's 24-bit retry ($4080DC5C) goes through a stub
asm: jmp     mm_ptr_stub:l   | was: tst.w (sp)+; bne.w $4080DDE0; bchg #0,$1EFC; move.w #1,-(sp); bra.s $4080DC3E

patches.name: mm: the handle dispatcher's 24-bit retry ($4080DCCE) goes through a stub
asm: jmp     mm_hdl_stub:l   | was: tst.w (sp)+; bne.s $4080DCE0; movea.l a1,a0; bchg #0,$1EFC; move.w #1,-(sp); bra.s $4080DC7E

patches.name: mm: pointer stub in the zero padding at 0x62A40: no 24-bit retry for a pointer above 16 MB in 32-bit mode
asm: tst.w   %sp@+          | the retry flag: 0 the first time the block check failed
bne.s   9f              | the retry failed too: return its error
tst.b   0xcb2:w          | MMU32Bit: is the 68k in 32-bit mode?
beq.s   1f              | 24-bit mode: retry as the ROM always did
btst    #0,0x1efc:w      | did the check that failed use the 32-bit block layout?
cmpa.l  #0x00ffffff,%a0 | a0 = the pointer as the caller gave it
bhi.s   9f              | above 16 MB: no 24-bit zone holds it, the 32-bit error stands
1:      bchg    #0,0x1efc:w      | the ROM's retry: the other layout ...
9:      jmp     mm_fail:l       | MemErr = d0, $1EFC restored, return

patches.name: mm: handle stub at 0x62A80: no 24-bit retry for a handle above 16 MB in 32-bit mode
asm: btst    #0,0x1efc:w      | the failed check used the 32-bit layout
cmpa.l  #0x00ffffff,%a1 | a1 = the handle as the caller gave it

patches.name: flop: the seek wrapper at $4086D4B0 goes through a stub (the 400K drive's speed)
asm: jmp     flop_stub:l     | was: bclr #11,d6; move.l JSeek,-(sp); rts

patches.name: flop: stub in the zero padding at 0x62AC0: the track to the Pi's window, the driver's speed-change wait for a new zone
asm: bclr    #11,%d6         | the wrapper's own first instruction
1:      cmp.l   #0x50534D42,(%a0) | 'PSMB': is the Pi's window there?
cmp.w   #0x5350,(%a0)   | 'SP': the kernel sets the 400K drive's speed on this board
addq.w  #1,4(%a0)       | one more seek: the kernel writes the speed of its zone
move.w  6(%a0),%d1      | the zone of the last seek
beq.s   9f              | the same zone: the speed stays
2:      mulu.w  8(%a0),%d1      | zones moved x the kernel's wait per zone (100 us units)
cmp.w   56(%a0),%d1     | no longer than the driver's longest speed wait
3:      cmp.w   20(%a0),%d1     | a longer wait already due stands
move.w  %d1,20(%a0)     | Seek waits it out for a 400K drive ($4086D512)
move.l  0x236:w,-(%sp)  | the wrapper's own: on to Seek through JSeek
